description.sw: Maswali ya ndiyo/hapana, maneno ya kuuliza: nani, nini, wapi, lini, jinsi gani, kwa nini, ngapi.
description.en: Yes/no questions, question words: who, what, where, when, how, why, how many.

label.sw: A. Sentensi rahisi — jozi 13 (kauli + swali + majibu)
label.en: A. Simple sentences — 13 pairs (statement + question + answers)

phrases.en: You are going home.

phrases.sw: Je, unaenda nyumbani? Ndiyo, ninaenda nyumbani. Hapana, siendi nyumbani.
phrases.en: Are you going home? Yes, I am going home. No, I am not going home.
Where are you going?
John is reading a book.

phrases.sw: Je, John anasoma kitabu? Ndiyo, John anasoma kitabu. Hapana, John hasomi kitabu.
phrases.en: Is John reading a book? Yes, John is reading a book. No, John is not reading a book.
What is John reading?
Anna is at home.

phrases.sw: Je, Anna yuko nyumbani? Ndiyo, Anna yuko nyumbani. Hapana, Anna hayuko nyumbani.
phrases.en: Is Anna at home? Yes, Anna is at home. No, Anna is not at home.
Where is Anna?
Grace sees a dog.

phrases.sw: Je, Grace anaona mbwa? Ndiyo, Grace anaona mbwa. Hapana, Grace haoni mbwa.
phrases.en: Does Grace see a dog? Yes, Grace sees a dog. No, Grace does not see a dog.
What does Grace see?
Daniel is eating rice.

phrases.sw: Je, Daniel anakula wali? Ndiyo, Daniel anakula wali. Hapana, Daniel hakuli wali.
phrases.en: Is Daniel eating rice? Yes, Daniel is eating rice. No, Daniel is not eating rice.
What is Daniel eating?
You know Grace.

phrases.sw: Je, mnajua Grace? Ndiyo, tunajua Grace. Hapana, hatujui Grace.
phrases.en: Do you know Grace? Yes, we know Grace. No, we do not know Grace.
Who do you know?
They are working in the field.

phrases.sw: Je, wanafanya kazi shambani? Ndiyo, wanafanya kazi shambani. Hapana, hawafanyi kazi shambani.
phrases.en: Are they working in the field? Yes, they are working in the field. No, they are not working in the field.
Where are they working?
John came yesterday.

phrases.sw: Je, John alikuja jana? Ndiyo, John alikuja jana. Hapana, John hakuja jana.
phrases.en: Did John come yesterday? Yes, John came yesterday. No, John did not come yesterday.
When did John come?
Anna is helping Daniel.

phrases.sw: Je, Anna anamsaidia Daniel? Ndiyo, Anna anamsaidia Daniel. Hapana, Anna hamsaidii Daniel.
phrases.en: Is Anna helping Daniel? Yes, Anna is helping Daniel. No, Anna is not helping Daniel.
Who is Anna helping?
Grace is writing a letter.

phrases.sw: Je, Grace anaandika barua? Ndiyo, Grace anaandika barua. Hapana, Grace haandiki barua.
phrases.en: Is Grace writing a letter? Yes, Grace is writing a letter. No, Grace is not writing a letter.
What is Grace writing?
You are not going home.

phrases.sw: Je, huendi nyumbani? Hapana, siendi nyumbani. Ndiyo, ninaenda nyumbani.
phrases.en: Are you not going home? No, I am not going home. Yes, I am going home.
Where are you going?
John did not eat today.

phrases.sw: Je, John hakula leo? Hapana, John hakula. Ndiyo, John alikula.
phrases.en: Did John not eat today? No, John did not eat. Yes, John ate.
What did John eat?
This is John's book.

phrases.sw: Je, hii ni kitabu cha John? Ndiyo, hiki ni kitabu chake. Hapana, hiki si kitabu chake.
phrases.en: Is this John's book? Yes, this is his book. No, this is not his book.
Whose book is this?

label.sw: B. Sentensi ngumu na za kuvutia zaidi — jozi 5
label.en: B. More complex and interesting sentences — 5 pairs

phrases.sw: John alisahau mwavuli wake kwa sababu alikuwa akikimbia kwenda kazini.
phrases.en: John forgot his umbrella because he was rushing to work.
Did John forget his umbrella? (yes/no)

phrases.sw: Kwa nini John alisahau mwavuli wake?
phrases.en: Why did John forget his umbrella?
Why was John rushing?

phrases.sw: Anna anapika chakula cha jioni kwa familia nzima kwa sababu leo ni siku ya kuzaliwa ya kaka yake.
phrases.en: Anna is cooking dinner for the whole family because today is her brother's birthday.

phrases.sw: Je, Anna anapika chakula cha jioni? (ndiyo/hapana)
phrases.en: Is Anna cooking dinner? (yes/no)

phrases.sw: Anna anapika chakula cha jioni kwa ajili ya nani?
phrases.en: Who is Anna cooking dinner for?

phrases.sw: Kwa nini Anna anapika chakula cha jioni?
phrases.en: Why is Anna cooking dinner?

phrases.sw: Daniel na Grace walikwenda sokoni kununua matunda na mboga.
phrases.en: Daniel and Grace went to the market to buy fruit and vegetables.

phrases.sw: Je, Daniel na Grace walikwenda sokoni? (ndiyo/hapana)
phrases.en: Did Daniel and Grace go to the market? (yes/no)
Where did Daniel and Grace go?

phrases.sw: Walikwenda sokoni kwa ajili ya nini?
phrases.en: Why did they go to the market?

phrases.sw: John anasimulia hadithi kuhusu mzee aliyeishi kijijini hapa miaka 50 iliyopita.
phrases.en: John is telling a story about an elder who lived in this village 50 years ago.
Is John telling a story? (yes/no)
Who is John telling a story about?
When did the elder live in this village?

phrases.sw: Anna hataki kwenda shambani kwa sababu anaogopa nyoka.
phrases.en: Anna does not want to go to the field because she is afraid of snakes.
Does Anna not want to go to the field? (yes/no)

phrases.sw: Kwa nini Anna hataki kwenda shambani?
phrases.en: Why does Anna not want to go to the field?
What is Anna afraid of?

label.sw: C. Maswali ya njia ya pili (indirect questions)

phrases.sw: John hajui Anna yuko wapi. Hajui yuko wapi.
phrases.en: John doesn't know where Anna is. He doesn't know where she is.
phrases.ctx_sw: swali lisilo la moja kwa moja — wapi

phrases.sw: Grace alimwuliza Daniel kwa nini mvua inanyesha. Daniel hajui kwa nini mvua inanyesha.
phrases.en: Grace asked Daniel why it is raining. Daniel doesn't know why it is raining.
phrases.ctx_sw: swali lisilo la moja kwa moja — kwa nini

phrases.sw: Anna haelewi John alifika sokoni vipi. Haelewi alifika vipi.
phrases.en: Anna doesn't understand how John got to the market. She doesn't understand how he got there.
phrases.ctx_sw: swali lisilo la moja kwa moja — vipi

label.sw: D. Maneno ya ziada ya kuuliza

phrases.en: How many books does John have?

phrases.sw: Nyumba ya Grace ina rangi gani?
phrases.en: What colour is Grace's house?
Whose book is this?

phrases.sw: Daniel alifika sokoni kwa miguu. Daniel alifika sokoni vipi?
phrases.en: Daniel walked to the market. How did Daniel get to the market?
Who is Anna going to the market with?

phrases.sw: John alikuja asubuhi. John alikuja lini? John alikuja saa ngapi?
phrases.en: John came in the morning. When did John come? What time did John come?

label.en: E. Five pairs with a story

phrases.en: The Goat in the Basket

phrases.sw: Anna na Grace walimtafuta mbuzi siku nzima lakini walimkuta tu jioni — alikuwa akilala kwenye kikapu cha nguo kama paka mdogo.
phrases.en: Anna and Grace were looking for the goat all day but only found it in the evening — it was sleeping in a basket of clothes like a kitten.

phrases.sw: Je, Anna na Grace walimkuta mbuzi? Ndiyo, walimkuta. Hapana, hawakumkuta.
phrases.en: Did Anna and Grace find the goat? Yes, they found the goat. No, they did not find the goat.
Where was the goat sleeping?

phrases.sw: Kwa nini mbuzi alikuwa akilala kwenye kikapu?
phrases.en: Why was the goat sleeping in the basket?
Who were they looking for all day?
The Stone That Glows

phrases.sw: Daniel alipata jiwe la ajabu barabarani ambalo linawaka usiku. Sasa majirani wote wanaomba amwonyeshe jiwe hilo lakini Daniel anaogopa kwamba wataiba.
phrases.en: Daniel found a strange stone on the road that glows at night. Now all the neighbours are asking him to show them the stone but Daniel is afraid that someone will steal it.

phrases.sw: Je, Daniel alipata jiwe? Ndiyo, Daniel alipata jiwe. Hapana, Daniel hakupata jiwe.
phrases.en: Did Daniel find a stone? Yes, Daniel found a stone. No, Daniel did not find a stone.
When does the stone glow?

phrases.sw: Kwa nini Daniel anaogopa kuonyesha jiwe?
phrases.en: Why is Daniel afraid to show the stone?
Who is asking Daniel to show the stone?
The Bird That Repeats Words

phrases.sw: Grace analisha ndege karibu na dirisha lake na majirani wote wanasema kwamba ndege huyu anaweza kurudia maneno kama kasuku. Lakini Grace ana uhakika kwamba ndege anapenda tu sauti yake.
phrases.en: Grace feeds a bird outside her window and all the neighbours say that this bird can repeat words like a parrot. But Grace is sure that the bird simply loves her voice.

phrases.sw: Je, Grace analisha ndege? Ndiyo, Grace analisha ndege. Hapana, Grace hamsishi ndege.
phrases.en: Does Grace feed a bird? Yes, Grace feeds a bird. No, Grace does not feed a bird.
What can the bird do?

phrases.sw: Kwa nini majirani wanazungumza kuhusu ndege?
phrases.en: Why do the neighbours talk about the bird?
What does Grace believe?
The Mango Rain

phrases.sw: Jana kulikuwa na upepo mkali kijijini na maembe mengi yaliyoiva yalianguka kutoka kwa mti mkubwa wa embe karibu na nyumba ya John hadi watoto wote walikusanya na kufanya sherehe. Sasa John kwa mzaha anauita mti huo "mkarimu".
phrases.en: Yesterday there was a strong wind in the village and so many ripe mangoes fell from the big mango tree by John's house that all the children collected them and had a celebration. Now John jokingly calls the tree "generous".

phrases.sw: Je, kulikuwa na upepo kijijini? Ndiyo, kulikuwa na upepo. Hapana, haukuwa na upepo.
phrases.en: Was there wind in the village? Yes, there was wind in the village. No, there was no wind in the village.
What fell from the tree?
Why did the children have a celebration?

phrases.sw: John sasa anauita mti huo nini?
phrases.en: What does John now call the tree?
The Forgotten Shoes

phrases.sw: John aliacha viatu vyake karibu na mto alipokuwa akiosha miguu yake na alipokuwa anarudi aliona kwamba kiatu kimoja kimetoweka. Ikabainika kwamba mbuzi alikicharua hadi kwenye zizi lake na sasa anakitafuna.
phrases.en: John left his shoes by the river when he was washing his feet and when he came back he saw that one shoe had disappeared. It turned out that a goat had carried it off to its pen and was now chewing on it.

phrases.sw: Je, John aliacha viatu vyake karibu na mto? Ndiyo, John aliacha viatu vyake. Hapana, John hakuacha viatu vyake.
phrases.en: Did John leave his shoes by the river? Yes, John left his shoes by the river. No, John did not leave his shoes by the river.
Where did the shoe disappear to?
Who took the shoe?

phrases.sw: Mbuzi anafanya nini na kiatu sasa?
phrases.en: What is the goat doing with the shoe now?

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 1. Jinsi maswali ya ndiyo/hapana yanavyoundwa
moderator_questions.en: Question 1. How yes/no questions are formed

body.sw:
Katika lugha mbalimbali maswali ya ndiyo/hapana yanajengwa tofauti.

Katika Kirusi lafudhi peke yake inatosha — "Ты идёшь домой." na "Ты идёшь домой?" — mpangilio wa maneno ni sawa, lafudhi peke yake inabadilika.

Katika Kiingereza kitenzi kinahamia mbele — "You are going home." → "Are you going home?" — mpangilio wa maneno unabadilika.

Katika Kiswahili chembe je inaongezwa mwanzoni — "Unaenda nyumbani." → "Je, unaenda nyumbani?" — mpangilio wa maneno haubadiliki lakini neno maalum linaonekana.

Katika Kijapani chembe ka inaongezwa mwishoni — "Uchi ni kaeru." → "Uchi ni kaeru ka?"

Angalia tafsiri zako za maswali rahisi ya ndiyo/hapana. Swali linajengwaje katika lugha yako?
body.en:
Different languages form yes/no questions in different ways.

In Russian intonation alone is enough — "Ты идёшь домой." and "Ты идёшь домой?" — the word order is the same, only the intonation changes.

In English the verb moves to the front — "You are going home." → "Are you going home?" — the word order changes.

In Swahili the particle je is added at the beginning — "Unaenda nyumbani." → "Je, unaenda nyumbani?" — the word order does not change but a special word appears.

In Japanese the particle ka is added at the end — "Uchi ni kaeru." → "Uchi ni kaeru ka?"

Look at your translations of the simple yes/no questions. How is a question formed in your language?

sw: Lafudhi peke yake — mpangilio wa maneno haubadiliki, hakuna maneno maalum
Mpangilio wa maneno unabadilika → unabadilika vipi hasa? Toa mfano
Chembe au neno maalum linaongezwa → lipi? Liko mwanzoni au mwishoni? Toa mfano
Mchanganyiko → eleza na utoe mifano
en: Intonation only — the word order does not change, no special words
The word order changes → how exactly? Give an example
A special particle or word is added → which one? Does it go at the beginning or at the end? Give an example
A combination → explain and give examples

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 2. Neno la kuuliza linasimama wapi
moderator_questions.en: Question 2. Where the question word stands

body.sw:
Katika Kirusi na Kiingereza neno la kuuliza linasimama mwanzoni mwa sentensi — "Куда ты идёшь?", "Where are you going?"

Katika baadhi ya lugha neno la kuuliza linasimama mahali pale ambapo jibu lingesimama — yaani katikati au mwishoni mwa sentensi. Kwa mfano katika Kichina: "Unaenda wapi?" badala ya "Wapi unaenda?"

Angalia tafsiri zako za sentensi zenye maneno ya kuuliza — wapi, nini, lini, kwa nini, nani, ngapi. Neno la kuuliza linasimama wapi katika lugha yako?
body.en:
In Russian and English the question word stands at the beginning of the sentence — "Куда ты идёшь?", "Where are you going?"

In some languages the question word stands in the same position as the answer would — that is in the middle or at the end of the sentence. For example in Chinese: "You are going where?" instead of "Where are you going?"

Look at your translations of phrases with question words — where, what, when, why, who, how many. Where does the question word stand in your language?

sw: Mwanzoni mwa sentensi — kama katika Kirusi
Mahali pa neno linalojibiwa — katikati au mwishoni
Tofauti kulingana na neno la kuuliza → eleza na utoe mifano
en: At the beginning of the sentence — like in Russian
In the position of the word it is asking about — in the middle or at the end
Differently depending on the question word → explain and give examples

body.sw:
Angalia tafsiri zako za:

- "Je, huendi nyumbani?"
- "Je, John hakula leo?"

Katika Kirusi swali la ukanushi linajengwa vivyo hivyo kama swali la kawaida — unaongeza tu "не" mbele ya kitenzi.

Katika Kiingereza ni ngumu zaidi — "Aren't you going home?" — ukanushi umejengwa ndani ya kitenzi kisaidizi.

Katika lugha yako — swali la ukanushi linajengwa vivyo hivyo kama swali la kawaida, tu na ukanushi uliongezwa? Au kuna muundo maalum?
body.en:
Look at your translations of:

- "Are you not going home?"
- "Did John not eat today?"

In Russian a negative question is formed the same way as a regular question — you simply add "не" before the verb.

In English it is more complex — "Aren't you going home?" — the negation is built into the auxiliary verb.

In your language — is a negative question formed the same way as a regular question, just with negation added? Or is there a special construction?

sw: Vivyo hivyo kama swali la kawaida pamoja na ukanushi
Muundo maalum → eleza na utoe mifano
en: The same as a regular question plus negation
A special construction → explain and give examples

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 4. Majibu ya ndiyo na hapana
moderator_questions.en: Question 4. The answers yes and no

body.sw:
Katika Kirusi "ndiyo" na "hapana" ni maneno tofauti ambayo hayabadiliki kamwe.

Katika baadhi ya lugha "ndiyo" na "hapana" yanabadilika kulingana na swali. Kwa mfano katika Kiwelsh — hakuna maneno tofauti ya "ndiyo" na "hapana", badala yake kitenzi kutoka swali kinajibiwa katika hali ya uthibitisho au ukanushi: "Je, unaenda?" → "Naenda" / "Siendi".

Katika baadhi ya lugha ukijibu swali la ukanushi "Je, huendi?" jibu "ndiyo" linamaanisha "ndiyo, siendi" — yaani linathibitisha ukanushi. Katika lugha nyingine "ndiyo" daima linamaanisha "naenda" bila kujali umbo la swali.

Angalia majibu uliyoandika katika tafsiri zako. "Ndiyo" na "hapana" zinafanya kazi vipi katika lugha yako?
body.en:
In Russian "yes" and "no" are separate words that never change.

In some languages "yes" and "no" change depending on the question. For example in Welsh — there are no separate words for "yes" and "no", instead the verb from the question is repeated in its positive or negative form: "Are you going?" → "Going" / "Not going".

In some languages when answering a negative question "Are you not going?" the answer "yes" means "yes, I am not going" — that is it confirms the negation. In other languages "yes" always means "I am going" regardless of the form of the question.

Look at the answers you wrote in your translations. How do "yes" and "no" work in your language?

sw: Maneno tofauti yasiyobadilika kama katika Kirusi
Umbo la kitenzi linajibiwa → toa mifano
Kuna kitu maalum na maswali ya ukanushi → eleza
en: Separate unchanging words like in Russian
The verb form is repeated → give examples
There is something special with negative questions → explain

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 5. Swali lisilo la moja kwa moja

body.sw:
Katika Kirusi swali la moja kwa moja — "Unaenda wapi?" — na swali lisilo la moja kwa moja — "Sijui unaenda wapi" — vinajengwa tofauti kidogo. Katika swali lisilo la moja kwa moja hakuna lafudhi ya kuuliza na wakati mwingine mpangilio wa maneno unabadilika.

Katika baadhi ya lugha maswali ya moja kwa moja na yasiyokuwa ya moja kwa moja yanajengwa vivyo hivyo. Katika nyingine — ni tofauti kabisa, na chembe maalum au maumbo ya kitenzi.

Angalia sentensi hii kutoka hadithi — "John hajui kwa nini mbuzi alikuwa akilala kwenye kikapu." Hili ni swali lisilo la moja kwa moja. Linajengwa vivyo hivyo kama swali la moja kwa moja katika lugha yako au tofauti?
body.en:
In Russian a direct question — "Where are you going?" — and an indirect question — "I don't know where you are going" — are built slightly differently. In the indirect question there is no question intonation and sometimes the word order changes.

In some languages direct and indirect questions are built the same way. In others they are completely different, with special particles or verb forms.

Look at this phrase from the stories — "John does not know why the goat was sleeping in the basket." This is an indirect question. Is it built the same way as a direct question in your language or differently?

sw: Vivyo hivyo kama swali la moja kwa moja
Tofauti → nini hasa kinabadilika? Toa mfano wa swali la moja kwa moja na lisilo la moja kwa moja pamoja
en: The same as a direct question
Differently → what exactly changes? Give an example of a direct and an indirect question side by side

moderator_questions.sw: Swali la 6. Kukusanya kitabu cha sarufi

body.sw: Kulingana na maudhui yote yaliyotolewa — tafsiri za sentensi na majibu ya maswali hapo juu — tunga kitabu kifupi cha sarufi kuhusu maswali katika lugha yako.
